title: Developing a Curriculum Committee Proposal for a New MA in Arts Administration
goal: Develop a curriculum committee proposal for a new Master of Arts in Arts Administration offered jointly by the Department of Theatre and Film and the College of Business.
occupation: Chair and associate professor in the department of theater and film

Step-1.step_name: Ask Claude to evaluate the need for a graduate program in Arts Administration by comparing programs in Alabama and the region, workforce demand, regional opportunities, and how the proposed degree could complement existing graduate offerings at Jax State.
Step-1.step_action: Research the degree and its potential, then strategizing how the degree could be implemented

nodes.label: Define research objective and compile comparison evidence
nodes.detail: Opens a new Claude chat, attaches five PDFs on regional Arts Administration programs (Troy, Indiana University, CSU Online, OU Online), and asks Claude to evaluate the need for an Arts Administration graduate program in Alabama comparing regional programs, workforce demand, and fit with Jax State's offerings.

nodes.label: Research and develop the Arts Administration needs assessment
nodes.detail: In response to the user's request, Claude researches regional Arts Administration programs, workforce and creative-economy data, tuition-reciprocity opportunities, and JSU's existing academic offerings. It synthesizes the evidence into a formal needs-assessment report, generates and visually verifies the Word document, and delivers the completed assessment with a summary of key findings and data limitations.

nodes.label: Review the response and delivered needs-assessment document and plan differentiation feedback
nodes.detail: Reads through the delivered document and begins composing feedback that the program needs a distinction from the Troy model, setting up the next request.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source a1: Requests a needs assessment for an Arts Administration graduate program
Target a2: Outputs the needs-assessment word doc.
Reasoning: User accepts the output.

Step-2.step_name: Internships and Program Differentiation from Other Institutions.
Step-2.step_action: Build innovative strategy of internships based around the program and working with the Randy Owen Center. This step is the proposal of what would make the program meaningfully different, including internships, summer intensive, and community partnerships

nodes.label: Request program differentiators leveraging JSU assets
nodes.detail: Proposes distinguishing the program from Troy's model via career-changer pathways, a 3+1 undergrad-to-MA option, an online component, and a component built around the newly opened Randy Owen Center for the Performing Arts (ROC) for internships and sponsorship work.

nodes.label: Research and incorporate JSU-specific program differentiators
nodes.detail: Claude researches the Randy Owen Center for the Performing Arts, JSU's Faster Master's accelerated-degree policy, and the university's online program infrastructure to ground the proposed differentiators in existing institutional mechanisms. It then updates the needs-assessment document with a new Differentiators section covering broader admission access, a 3+1 pathway, an online/hybrid track, and ROC integration with specific courses and practicum opportunities, verifies the revised document, and delivers the updated file.

nodes.label: Review the Arts Administration needs assessment
Review the updated Arts Administration needs assessment
Request a low-residency redesign
nodes.detail: Asks to replace the 'no arts degree required' prerequisite-coursework idea with a low-residency option where career-changers take intensive graduate courses in their chosen discipline.

nodes.label: Research and incorporate a low-residency program model
nodes.detail: Claude researches low-residency arts-graduate program precedents, including a comparable low-residency Cultural Administration program, then redesigns the needs assessment around a unified low-residency model. It replaces the prerequisite-coursework concept with discipline-specific immersive intensives, connects the online pathway and ROC programming to the same structure, updates related sections of the document, rebuilds and verifies the revised report, and delivers the updated file.

nodes.label: Review revised differentiators

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source b1: Requests program differentiators
Target b6: Outputs the needs assessment redesigned 
Reasoning: b2 adds a Differentiators section, b5 asks for low residency, user rereads (b4) while b6 generating, then accepts b6.

Step-3.step_action: Basing the curriculum in what we currently have and what is planned, build a proposed curriculum for a 3+1, 4+1, and traditional masters program.

nodes.label: Request draft curriculum built from existing JSU courses
nodes.detail: Asks Claude to propose a draft curriculum for the 3+1, 4+1, and traditional master's using as many existing Jax State courses as possible, attaching the 2025-2026 graduate and undergraduate catalogs.

nodes.label: Develop a draft curriculum using existing JSU courses
nodes.detail: Claude processes the graduate and undergraduate catalogs and systematically identifies relevant existing courses across Public Administration, Social Work, Marketing, Public History, Organizational Communication, Theatre, Art, and Music. Using these courses, it designs a 36-credit curriculum with a Public Administration core, Arts Administration functional core, discipline electives, and a ROC-based capstone, and begins incorporating the curriculum into the needs-assessment document. Claude encounters a rendering issue and reaches its tool-use limit before rebuilding and verifying the revised document, then summarizes the proposed curriculum and asks the user whether to continue.

nodes.label: Review Claude's draft curriculum proposal

Step-4.step_action: IDentify areas of need for new courses and brainstorm new Arts Administration graduate courses. Determine which existing MBA or business courses could be shared across programs.

nodes.label: Push back on undergraduate course-level conversion and grant-writing course fit
nodes.detail: Reads Claude's mid-task summary, then points out that the undergraduate-level courses named (MU 357, ART 484/486, THR 349) can't themselves count toward a master's and would need graduate-level numbers, and questions whether the Social Work grant-writing course is the right fit versus a dedicated arts fundraising course.

nodes.label: Revise the curriculum using graduate directed-studies courses
nodes.detail: Claude investigates existing graduate directed-studies and topics-based course shells as a way to address the user's concerns, identifying options in Music, Art, Theatre, and Public Administration. It then revises the curriculum to use these graduate-level shells with arts-specific topic designations, replaces the Social Work grant-writing course with PA 5885 focused on fundraising and development for the arts, rebuilds and verifies the document, and delivers the revised version.

nodes.label: Review the revised curriculum with graduate directed-studies courses
Reject the directed-studies workaround and demand genuine new-course proposals
nodes.detail: Reads the directed-studies explanation and rejects it as too light a lift, stating the courses mentioned will need the heavier catalog process of real new course numbers rather than independent studies.

nodes.label: Develop and incorporate genuine new-course proposals into the curriculum
nodes.detail: Claude designs five new 5000-level course proposals, checks the proposed course numbers against the existing catalog for conflicts, and revises the curriculum around the new courses. It updates the needs assessment to clarify that 27 of 36 credit hours use existing courses while 9 hours require five new-course proposals, verifies the revised document, and delivers the updated version.

nodes.label: Review the revised curriculum with new-course proposals

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source c1: Requests to draft a curriculum from existing JSU courses.
Target d5: Outputs the revised curriculum with five new courses
Reasoning:d1 and d4 reject undergraduate and directed-study workarounds (refinements), user accepts d5

nodes.label: Request a separate document with detailed descriptions for the new courses
nodes.detail: Reviews the delivered document, then asks for a new, separate document that crafts full course descriptions for the five new courses that need to be proposed.

nodes.label: Develop and deliver detailed new-course proposals
nodes.detail: Claude creates a separate new-course-proposals document for the five proposed courses, providing catalog-style descriptions, course details, relationships to existing coursework, needs-based justifications, and student learning outcomes. It visually verifies the completed document, delivers it, and flags remaining issues including unassigned instructors and the greater approval burden for proposed graduate courses based on 300-level undergraduate counterparts.

nodes.label: Final review of the delivered course-proposals document in Word
nodes.detail: Downloads and opens JSU_Arts_Administration_New_Course_Proposals.docx directly in Microsoft Word, browses the Navigation pane heading outline for each of the five courses, and reads through the PA 5886 justification and learning-outcomes text, with no further Claude interaction for the rest of the session.

user_response.label: adopt
user_response.reasoning:
Source d7: Requests a separate document describing the courses
Target d8: Outputs 'JSU_arts administration new course proposals.docx'.
Reasoning: User opens and reads it in Word. Accepted.
